facts.raw_span: A female infant with history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
was admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
Seventeen days after her last day of chemotherapy, while neutropenic, she became febrile
Patient had an indwelling catheter
Several vesicles with an erythematous base were observed on the lower back and left thigh
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
Periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and varicella zoster virus (VZV) were negative
CT scan with contrast of thorax and brain showed lesions in the liver and brain

support_spans: Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis

concepts.why: The presence of filamentous bacilli with septa and gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis, along with negative PCR testing for HSV and VZV, supports the diagnosis of Bacillus cereus infection.

support_spans: Seventeen days after her last day of chemotherapy, while neutropenic, she became febrile
Patient had an indwelling catheter
Several vesicles with an erythematous base were observed on the lower back and left thigh
contradict_spans: Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
concepts.why: The patient's neutropenic state, presence of an indwelling catheter, and observation of vesicles with an erythematous base support the diagnosis of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, although the histopathology results argue against it.

support_spans: Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
Periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
concepts.why: The presence of filamentous bacilli with septa and gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis, along with negative periodic acid-Schiff staining for fungal elements, supports the diagnosis of Nocardia infection.
It explains the presence of lesions in the liver and brain as seen on the CT scan, which is consistent with disseminated Nocardia infection.

rationales.F05: Vesicles with an erythematous base are consistent with cutaneous manifestations of bacterial infections such as Bacillus cereus or Nocardia.
rationales.F06: Filamentous bacilli with septa are characteristic of Nocardia infection, and also consistent with Bacillus cereus.
rationales.F07: Gram-variable rods are consistent with Nocardia or Bacillus cereus, but less typical for Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is usually gram-negative.
rationales.F10: Disseminated infection with lesions in the liver and brain is more typical of Nocardia, especially in the context of immunocompromised patients.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of hematoxylin-eosin stain showing focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa and gram stain revealing numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis decided it.
